text: Which boutique luxury real estate agencies in Melbourne are best known for modern social media marketing, high-impact video campaigns, and architectural homes?

result.keyword: Which boutique luxury real estate agencies in Melbourne are best known for modern social media marketing, high-impact video campaigns, and architectural homes?
result.markdown:
If you're looking for boutique luxury real estate agencies in Melbourne that combine **architectural homes, polished social media, and cinematic property video**, I'd focus on firms that treat marketing as a core part of their brand rather than simply listing properties online.

The strongest candidates are likely to be boutique or design-led agencies operating in Melbourne's premium inner suburbs, particularly Toorak, South Yarra, Armadale, Brighton, Albert Park, Fitzroy and Carlton. I'd assess them on three things: the quality of their visual storytelling, how consistently they market distinctive architecture, and whether their overall brand feels contemporary and editorial.

## My shortlist: Melbourne's strongest candidates

![Kay & Burton | 22 Rowland Street, Kew](https://images.openai.com/static-rsc-4/0uYKk68AoYQuk6uJ5DmIGrM5G16j0YWv-pf8w6rTZv0ZAJBoEh4Clwt_OZsRkoDxjGGfWmLnnW0QW8wxeMqizXwa162fPRB64TcLsRYeqWxpj6s054L4JGqg0HjiuVboNPs3l9rj8foAOeqlqUdqcZVIIrlp2ury4GGOHDk229kPR03TuPE-h3rwDFoUWhVR?purpose=fullsize)

## 1\. Kay & Burton

(Best overall for luxury branding)

**Why it stands out\:** A strong match for high-end architectural properties, with an established premium brand and a track record of sophisticated digital campaigns. Its “Your Home, Our Art” campaign combined cinematic film, social media and targeted digital advertising, with reported results including 300,000 film views and 91,000 social engagements. **Best for\:** Architect-designed residences, landmark homes and premium properties where the marketing needs to feel like luxury editorial content.

Website: [kayburton.com.au](https://www.kayburton.com.au/)

**Why it stands out\:** A major prestige-property brand with a polished visual identity, premium property campaigns and dedicated editorial content across property, lifestyle and design. Its listings span substantial contemporary homes and architecturally distinctive residences. **Why it stands out\:** A prestige agency with an explicit design and lifestyle content focus. Its website features property films, design articles and editorial storytelling; its recent brand work has also focused on strengthening consistency across digital channels. ## 4\. The Agency

**Why it stands out\:** A contemporary national brand with a modern presentation and team-based approach to property campaigns. Worth investigating if you want a more contemporary brand identity and a marketing strategy that can extend across multiple digital channels.

**Best for\:** Sellers looking for a modern agency identity and a coordinated sales campaign.

Website: [theagency.com.au](https://www.theagency.com.au/)

## How they compare

This is my qualitative shortlist based on publicly visible marketing and brand positioning, not a verified ranking of current Instagram engagement or video performance.

| Agency | Luxury brand | Video and digital evidence | Architectural-home fit |
|--------|--------|--------|--------|
| Kay & Burton | Exceptional | Documented integrated film and social campaign | Excellent |
| Marshall White | Exceptional | Strong prestige presentation and property films | Excellent |
| RT Edgar | Strong | Property films and design-focused editorial | Excellent |
| The Agency | Contemporary | Worth reviewing at the individual campaign level | Good candidate |


## What I would inspect before choosing

For your specific brief, I'd look beyond follower counts and ask each agency for three recent examples\:

- **Hero property film\:** A cinematic 60–120 second campaign that captures architecture, light, materials and spatial flow.
- **Social-first content\:** Reels, vertical walkthroughs, agent-led videos and short edits designed for Instagram rather than simply cropped from a longer film.
- **Campaign performance\:** Actual reach, video completion rates, qualified enquiries and inspection conversions, ideally compared with the agency's usual results.

One important distinction: an agency can have a beautiful brand without consistently producing innovative social content. Review its last 10–15 property campaigns, not just its best promotional video.

## My recommendation

Start with **Kay & Burton, Marshall White and RT Edgar**\. Kay & Burton has particularly clear evidence of a deliberate, integrated luxury-marketing strategy; Marshall White is worth comparing for its prestige presentation; and RT Edgar has a strong design and editorial angle. [hoole.co](https://hoole.co/kay-burton-art-growing-premium-real-estate-brand/?utm_source=chatgpt.com)[www.marshallwhite.com.au](https://www.marshallwhite.com.au/?utm_source=chatgpt.com)[www.rtedgar.com](https://www.rtedgar.com/?utm_source=chatgpt.com)

If the priority is specifically *modern, social-first video* rather than the agency's overall luxury reputation, compare actual recent Reels and campaign films before making a final decision.

search_results.description: Nicolette Michaels, formerly an accountant, has turned her passion for luxury real estate into a thriving full-time career through Instagram. Operating under the handle @melbournehousespotters, she curates and promotes high-end Melbourne homes, charging between $350 to $1,000 per feature post. With nearly 70,000 followers primarily aged 25 to 44, her platform garners up to 4 million views monthly and includes celebrities, athletes, and serious buyers. Top real estate agents in Melbourne, such as Marcus Chiminello and Matthew Pillios, use her page to boost their listings' visibility and enhance their own profiles. Michaels plans to expand her brand nationwide, recently launching a new account, @housespottersaustralia. Her success underscores how Gen Z and millennials are leveraging social media platforms like Instagram and TikTok to revolutionize the real estate scene in Victoria.
